...RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. O MAHESH, ADVOCATE FOR R3  R1 - NOTICE DISPENSED WITH V/O DATED 20.11.2017  R2 - SERVED)
 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 22.08.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.138/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, KADUR, CHIKMAGALUR DISTRICT, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation as well as questioning the 50% of contributory negligence fastened on the appellant/claimant.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 04.02.2011 at about 9.00 p.m., near Fire Station in Kadur Town between the vehicles i.e., motorcycle bearing No.KA.16/S-2449 and Mahindra Maxima vehicle bearing No.KA-13/A-7158.

Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of IMV Act,
seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the Tribunal has awarded meagre amount of compensation.
Hence, prays for enhancement of compensation.
Further, it is submitted that holding of 50% of contributory negligence on the part of the appellant/claimant because of he was not having driving license is not correct.
The driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle was driving with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle of the claimant and for which, the claimant has not contributed any negligence to the accident.
Therefore, just because the claimant was not having driving license is not a ground to make contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
Therefore, prays for modification of the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

Further, it is submitted that even though respondent No.1 was not having driving license and owner is liable but the claimant being third party, therefore, the Insurance Company has to satisfy the claim and then recover the compensation amount from the owner.

Therefore, prays for modification T C Kenchappa vs Thrinesha on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88177514/
2 of the award on all these grounds.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company submitted that in the present case, the Mahindra Maxima vehicle was not having driving licence and he was charge sheeted for not holding driving licence.
Therefore, the Insurance Company has proved that respondent No.1 was not having driving license.

Further, it is submitted that since the claimant was also not having driving license,
hence, it is amounting to driving the vehicle by an inexperienced person also makes contribution to the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in holding the claimant has also contributed 50%
rash and negligence.
Accordingly, awarded 50% determined compensation by fastening the liability on respondent No.2-owner.

Therefore, justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
6.
In the present case, the claimant was driving the motorcycle and respondent No.1 was driving the Mahindra Maxima vehicle.
It is alleged in the complaint that the driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle was driving the same with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle.

Consequently,
upon investigation, the charge sheet is filed against respondent No.1 - driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle.
Just because the claimant was not having driving license that cannot be ground to say that the claimant has contributed 50% rash and negligent driving and caused the accident.
Non-holding of driving licence may be a factor to say that the rider of the motorcycle may be an inexperienced person but that alleged cannot be fundamental reason for the accident.

When upon statutory investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle and also in the complaint and evidence, it is revealed that the driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle had caused the accident.
Therefore, holding contributory negligence on part of the claimant to the extent 50% is not correct.
Therefore, it is proved that the driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle was entirely responsible for the accident.
Therefore, the contributory negligence fastened on the claimant is set aside.

7. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation as follows:
 Sl.No Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
 .
1 . Pain and sufferings 15,000.00  2.
Medical expenses 5,000.00  3. Conveyance/Traveling 5,000.00  expenses
4. Attendant charges and 5,000.00  nutritious food  5. Loss of income 8,000.00  6. Discomfort and loss of 5,000.00  amenities of life
T C Kenchappa vs Thrinesha on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88177514/
3 8. As per the medical evidence produced before the Court, it is proved that the claimant has suffered fracture of both bones of left lower third forearm which is grievous in nature.
The doctor has not been examined.
There is no evidence that the claimant had suffered disability affecting his work.
The claimant is a agriculturist of aged 45 years.
Therefore, the compensation awarded under the head 'pain and sufferings' is on the lower side.
Hence, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is enhanced under the said head.
9. The claimant has not produced any evidence to prove how much expenditure incurred towards medical expenses but awarded the compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses.
The same is kept in tact.
There is no record to show how many days the claimant was in hospital for treatment.

Therefore, the compensation of Rs.5,000/- granted under the head 'conveyance/travelling expenses,
etc.' is kept in tact and also for 'attendant charges, nourishment, etc.' is kept in tact.
The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.8,000/- under the head 'loss of income' which is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.
Since the claimant must not have attended the work for two months considering the nature of injuries.
Accordingly, for two months, the loss of income is awarded at Rs.15,000/- as above stated.
Further, the compensation of Rs.5,000/- awarded under the head 'discomfort and loss of amenities of life' is on the lesser side.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is enhanced under the said head.

10. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:
 Sl.No Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
 .
1 . Pain and sufferings 20,000.00  2.

Medical expenses 5,000.00  3. Conveyance/Traveling 5,000.00  expenses  4. Attendant charges and 5,000.00  nutritious food  5. Loss of income 15,000.00  6. Discomfort and loss of 15,000.00  amenities of life
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.21,500/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.65,000/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.43,500/- (Rs.65,000 - Rs.21,500) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
12. In the present case, it is proved that the driver of the Mahindra Maxima vehicle was not having driving license.
Therefore, respondent No.2 - the owner is liable to pay the compensation.

4
Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation because of breach of policy conditions.
But the claimant is a third party to the Mahindra Maxima vehicle, therefore, as per Section 149(2) of the MV Act, the Insurance Company has successfully established the defence.

Therefore, the Insurance Company as if judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in favour of the claimant, as per - 10 - Sub-Sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of MV Act and also as per the principles of law down in the cases of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Swaran Singh1, Pappuu and others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another2, and full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co., Ltd., vs.
Yallavva and another3, principle of pay and recovery is applied since the claimant is a third party.

Hence, an order of pay and recovery is made.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.138/2011 is hereby modified holding the reported in 2004 ACJ 1 reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 reported in ILR 2020 KAR 2239 - 11 - claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.43,500/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The Insurance Company shall pay the above said compensation at the first instance then recover it from the owner of the offending vehicle.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.
The claimant is not entitled interest for the period between order of issuance of notice to respondent for the first time till the copy of the appeal memorandum was served on the Insurance Company on 05.09.2022.
During this period, the claimant is not entitled for interest on the above determined compensation.
